# Extra Life adaptive probabilities — Intake Brief (AH-0MW8178ZR0090CNY)

## Original request (verbatim)

> Create a minor increase in the probabiliyt of an extra life power up being dropped as the player loses lives. It should not be noticable, but the player should "feel lucky" when one drops and they are low on lives. This, presumably means the amount of increase is exponential as the player drops to only 1 life left. Also ensure that a mini-boss kill *always* leaves an extra life power up.

> **Producer answers received (this intake):** Q1 → **(a)** scale the
> `extra_life` weight in the existing weighted pool; Q2 → **(a)** always spawn
> a physical `extra_life` field pickup at the death position, in addition to the
> wheel reward, even at the life cap / full slots; Q3 → a **gentler curve than
> the offered (b): `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives** (i.e. a multiplier of
> **`2^livesLost`**). Asteroid clarification: small asteroids **no longer drop
> lives** at shipped defaults — see "Existing state" below.

## Problem statement

Extra Life currently drops at one fixed rate for the whole run, regardless of
how many lives the player has left. A player down to their last life therefore
gets no extra recovery help, and the moment an Extra Life appears never feels
like a lucky break. Separately, defeating a bespoke mini-boss — the biggest
scheduled highlight of every level — never leaves a life on the field, so the
encounter has no guaranteed survivability payoff.

## Users

- **Players** — want a subtle, invisible-to-them safety net that makes an Extra
  Life feel like a lucky break exactly when they are low on lives, and want a
  mini-boss kill to reliably restore a life.
- **Designers / balance tuners** — need the adaptive curve and the mini-boss
  guarantee expressed as named, persisted tunables (not scattered magic
  numbers) so the feel can be retuned without code changes.
- **Developers / AI agents** — need the rule defined once in the shared core so
  the game and every gym cannot drift apart (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a **player on my last life**, I want an Extra Life to drop a little more
  often than usual, so I get a genuine chance to turn a doomed run around —
  without ever noticing the game is helping me.
- As a **player who just beat a mini-boss**, I want the wreck to always leave
  an Extra Life, so the hardest fight in the level reliably pays back a life.
- As a **designer**, I want the adaptive curve in one tunable place so I can
  soften or sharpen the "lucky" feeling without touching gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Adaptive mechanism (one shared rule):** Extra Life drop
      propensity scales with the player's remaining lives by scaling the
      `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill drop pool**
      (the total per-kill drop chance is unchanged; Extra Life simply becomes a
      larger share of the drops that do occur). The multiplier is exactly
      `1×` at or above the run's starting lives and is monotonically
      non-decreasing as lives fall. The rule lives once in a shared pure helper
      consumed by both `PlayScene` and every drop-bearing gym.
- [ ] **AC2 — Curve is `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives:** the multiplier is
      `2 ** livesLost`, where `livesLost = max(0, runStartingLives − lives)`
      (`runStartingLives` defaults to 3; a hangar deployment may override it).
      So `≥3` lives → `1×`, `2` lives → `2×`, `1` life → `4×` (and `3` lives
      per the formula). The multiplier is applied to the weight; because the
      weighted pool is normalised, the resulting *probability* uplift is
      slightly below the weight ratio — an intentional extra layer of
      subtlety. At 2 lives the increase is modest ("not noticeable"); at 1 life
      it is a clear but still small uplift.
- [ ] **AC3 — Statistically verifiable:** a seeded simulation (N ≥ 10 000
      representative kills per lives value, documented seed set) demonstrates
      that the Extra Life drop rate at 2 lives and 1 life strictly exceeds the
      full-lives baseline and follows the documented weight-multiplier curve
      within tolerance; the test does not depend on a single lucky seed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Mini-boss always drops one:** every mini-boss defeat spawns
      exactly one `extra_life` **field pickup** at/near the mini-boss death
      position, **in addition to** the existing spin-the-wheel reward, in
      `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`. It spawns even at the 5-life cap and with a
      full slot pool; the normal drop separation nudge applies, and the existing
      six-slot collection gate and 5-life cap still govern pickup (a drop at the
      cap is simply not useful, but is still spawned).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tunables + persistence:** the curve constant (exponential base,
      default 2) and the starting-lives reference live in `GameRules` with
      documented defaults, clamped on load, and older rules blobs load
      unchanged. The adaptive multiplier composes with the existing level
      scaling (`powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`) and is applied after
      it, so the curve can never rise with campaign level.
- [ ] **AC6 — Parity & no duplicate implementation:** the rule exists once in a
      shared module and is consumed by the game and the gyms (including
      `GymMiniBoss` for the guaranteed drop); the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
      (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests:** unit tests cover the curve (`1×` at full lives,
      `2×` at 2, `4×` at 1, monotonic, clamping/guards), the mini-boss guarantee
      (exactly one `extra_life` spawned per defeat, game + gym), and the seeded
      distribution; the changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** the GDD §4.4 (Extra Life drop), §3.3.1 / §4.4.4
      (mini-boss defeat/reward — which today state the sweep is cosmetic and the
      wheel is the single reward), the game-rules documentation and code
      comments are updated, including any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who is down to their last life quietly sees Extra Life drops a little
more often — enough to feel lucky, never enough to notice — and every mini-boss
kill now reliably leaves one on the field.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (`AGENTS.md`; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`): the rule
  lives once in the shared core and is consumed by `PlayScene` and the relevant
  gym scenes (`GymFormationScene`, `GymMiniBoss`, and any asteroid/level gym
  that rolls Extra Life). No divergent copies.
- **Subtlety is a hard requirement:** the curve must not make Extra Life
  common; the player must not be able to perceive the manipulation.
- **No new art/assets:** reuse the existing `extra_life` code-drawn icon and
  shared drop pipeline.
- **Do not regress the deliberate supply reduction:** AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM halved the supply dial and turned the asteroid
  Extra-Life roll off. The adaptive uplift must be layered on top, not undo
  that tuning.
- **Extra Life stays field-pickup-only:** it must not leak back onto the
  hold-full choice or the mini-boss wheel (§4.4.4). The guaranteed mini-boss
  drop is a field pickup, not a wheel wedge.

## Existing state

- **Generic per-kill drop:** `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the
  level-resolved per-kill chance `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (0.09 at
  level 1 → 0.025 at level 10), then draws one kind from the shared weighted
  pool via `_drawNextDrop` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`,
  `CombatCoreScene._buildDefaultDropSpawner`). The spawner is built once at
  scene start with fixed weights; there is no per-kill weight adjustment today.
- **Extra Life weight:** fixed `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT = 3` in
  `src/core/rules.ts` (`defaultPowerUpWeights()`), against 4 for standard
  power-ups and 2 for the rare Smart Bomb / Orbital Strike. It never varies
  with lives.
- **Lives:** `GameState.lives` (start 3, cap `MAX_LIVES = 5` from the Extra
  Life catalogue entry). `Player`/HUD read the same value; the scene has
  `this.gameState.lives` at kill time.
- **Asteroid Extra Life roll — currently OFF:** `rollAsteroidExtraLife` +
  `extraLifeDropChance(level, rules)` in `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`
  is **disabled at shipped defaults**
  (`DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE = 0`, set by AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM). **So no, asteroids no longer drop lives.** The rule, the
  `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` key and its clamping/persistence are retained
  so a designer can re-enable the roll with one config value; when they do, the
  adaptive multiplier defined here composes with it (at the default `0` there is
  no behaviour change).
- **Mini-boss defeat:** `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` → `miniBoss.destroy()` runs
  the cosmetic death sweep (no drops, no score, no telemetry) and opens the
  spin-the-wheel reward (§4.4.4). Extra Life is deliberately excluded from the
  wheel. Consequently a mini-boss kill currently leaves **no** Extra Life.
- **Gym consumers:** `GymFormationScene` (`_rollExtraLifeDrop`), `GymLevel`,
  `GymMiniBoss` — the first two already call the shared asteroid roll; the
  mini-boss gym exercises the reward wheel.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared, pure **life-adaptive Extra Life weight multiplier**
   (`2 ** livesLost`, clipped to `≥ 1` and `1×` at/above the run's starting
   lives) and apply it to the `extra_life` weight in the shared weighted
   per-kill drop draw. At full lives the behaviour is byte-for-byte today's; at
   2 lives the likelihood doubles and at 1 life it quadruples, so the player
   "feels lucky" at 1 life without noticing at 2.
2. Make **every mini-boss defeat always spawn one `extra_life` field pickup**
   at/near the death position, on top of the wheel reward, in `PlayScene` and
   `GymMiniBoss`, regardless of the life cap or slot occupancy.
3. Express the curve as named, persisted `GameRules` tunables with documented
   defaults and load-time clamping.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the adaptive-curve tunable (exponential base,
  default 2; starting-lives reference) to `GameRules`, defaults, clamping,
  schema-compatible load.
- `src/core/livesScaling.ts` **(new)** — the pure life→weight-multiplier helper
  (single source of truth), beside `levelScaling.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — expose the
  Extra-Life weight adjustment through the shared drop draw so game + gyms
  share it (e.g. set the `extra_life` weight before each draw).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — apply the multiplier at kill time
  (`_maybeDropPowerUp`) and spawn the guaranteed Extra Life on mini-boss defeat
  (`_damageMiniBoss` / `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume the shared multiplier
  (full-lives baseline in a gym with no run).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — consume the guaranteed mini-boss drop
  (gym has no run lives: unconditional, matching the game's "always").
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/core/livesScaling.test.ts` **(new)**,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.miniboss*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §3.3.1 / §4.4.4 wording.

## Related work

- **Add an extra life power up (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3)** — introduced P8 Extra
  Life (passive +1, cap 5, rarer than standard drops). Completed.
- **Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S)** — added the small-asteroid
  Extra-Life roll (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`, `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`),
  later turned off by AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM. Completed.
- **Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene
  (AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X)** — wired `powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`
  into the kill path. Completed.
- **Level-scaling curves (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X)** — `src/core/levelScaling.ts`,
  the supply dial this feature composes with.
- **Supply-dial reduction / asteroid roll off (AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR,
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM)** — deliberate supply tightening; do not undo.
- **Mini-boss defeat sweep (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)** — cosmetic sweep, no drops.
- **Mini-Boss Reward — Spin the Wheel (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)** — the encounter's
  current single reward; Extra Life is field-pickup-only and excluded from the
  wheel. The guaranteed drop in this item must not change that exclusion.
- **Bot prioritises extra lives (AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4)** — the demo brain already
  prefers a live Extra Life pickup below the cap; unaffected but retested.
- **Duplicate check:** no completed item satisfies this brief's ACs. The
  closest completed items (above) implement fixed-rate Extra Life drops and the
  mini-boss reward; neither adapts the rate to lives nor guarantees a
  mini-boss Extra Life. No duplicate found.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Perceptibility risk (highest):** a curve tuned too high is noticeable and
  undermines the "not noticeable" requirement. The chosen `1×/2×/4×` curve is
  deliberately gentle; verify with a seeded statistical test and keep the base
  in `GameRules` for retuning.
- **Compounding with level scaling:** the supply dial already lowers drop
  chance with campaign level. The adaptive multiplier is applied after level
  scaling so a late-campaign player on 1 life still gets the intended uplift.
- **Weight vs probability:** the multiplier scales the *weight*, so the
  resulting probability uplift is slightly below the weight ratio because the
  pool normalises. This is intentional subtlety; the statistical test asserts
  the resulting *probability* ordering, not just the weight.
- **Mini-boss drop at the cap:** a guaranteed drop at 5 lives or with a full
  slot pool may be useless. Producer answer Q2(a): **still spawn it** —
  "always" is literal; the six-slot gate and life cap handle collection.
- **Gym semantics:** gyms have no run lives. `GymMiniBoss` always spawns the
  guaranteed drop; the adaptive multiplier uses the catalogue starting lives
  (3) as the baseline in gyms, so parity tests are deterministic.
- **Asteroid roll is off:** the multiplier's composition with the asteroid roll
  has no visible effect at the shipped default (`0`); it is defined for
  consistency if a designer re-enables the roll.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not add a HUD "pity counter", a visible luck meter,
  or extra-life bounties here — record any such idea as a linked work item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which drop channel should adapt? (mechanism)**
  - (a) Scale the `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill
    pool** (drop frequency unchanged; Extra Life becomes a larger share of the
    existing drops as lives fall).
  - (b) Add a separate independent Extra Life roll per kill.
  - (c) Raise the overall per-kill drop chance when low on lives.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — What does "mini-boss kill always leaves an extra life power up" mean
  exactly?**
  - (a) Always spawn a physical `extra_life` **field pickup** at the death
    position, in addition to the wheel reward, even at the cap / full slots.
  - (b) Same, but only when below the life cap.
  - (c) Add Extra Life as a wheel wedge/outcome instead of a field pickup.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Curve shape, magnitude, and interaction with level scaling.**
  - (a) `multiplier = base ** livesLost` (base ≈ 2.5–3 offered).
  - (b) A gentler/other curve or a per-lives table (e.g. `1× / 2× / 5×`).
  - (c) Also compose the multiplier into the asteroid Extra-Life roll.
  - **Answer (producer): an even gentler curve than (b) — `1× / 2× / 4×` at
    `3 / 2 / 1` lives.** This is exactly `multiplier = 2 ** livesLost`. For
    (c), the producer's follow-up question ("Asteroids no longer drop lives, do
    they?") was answered: the asteroid Extra-Life roll is **off at shipped
    defaults** (`0`), so there is no live asteroid source today; the shared
    multiplier is nonetheless defined once and applied to every Extra Life
    source so it composes if the roll is re-enabled (no behaviour change at
    `0`). Source: interactive reply + repository inspection
    (`src/core/rules.ts:341`, `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** – Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (completed)
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and on-screen pickups (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3** – Add an extra life power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvlisu03006wdod, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm (+499 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1, ac2 (+469 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1 (+427 more)

# Add regression tests for pulse-wave lifecycle and constant-stroke render

## Problem

No automated tests cover the pulse-wave lifecycle: supersede, range exit, boss destroy, or constant-stroke render policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least one new or extended automated test covers the wave lifecycle (supersede, range exit, boss destroy) and the constant-stroke render path.
- Supersede test: fire two volleys inside one wave lifetime; assert exactly one wave sprite in the display list.
- Range exit test: let a wave reach the edge of the screen; assert zero wave sprites in the display list.
- Boss destroy test: destroy the boss; assert zero wave sprites remain.
- Constant-stroke test: assert that the wave Graphics object uses a constant line width regardless of radius.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- src/entities/Boss.test.ts — new or extended tests for wave lifecycle.
data.title: Add regression tests for pulse-wave lifecycle and constant-stroke render

# Effort and Risk Report

## Effort Estimate

- **T-shirt size:** Medium
- **Three-point (PERT):** O=10.00h, M=18.00h, P=29.00h
- **Expected (E=(O+4M+P)/6):** 18.50h
- **Recommended (with overheads):** 27.50h
- **Range:** [19.00h — 38.00h]
- **Unit:** hours

### Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

| # | Item | O (h) | M (h) | P (h) | Expected (h) |
|---|------|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | Shared life-adaptive multiplier + GameRules tunable/defaults/clamping | 2.00 | 3.00 | 5.00 | 3.17 |
| 2 | Wire multiplier into shared drop draw + PlayScene kill path | 2.00 | 4.00 | 7.00 | 4.17 |
| 3 | Guaranteed mini-boss Extra Life field drop (PlayScene + GymMiniBoss) | 2.00 | 4.00 | 6.00 | 4.00 |
| 4 | Tests: curve unit, seeded distribution, mini-boss guarantee, parity guard | 3.00 | 5.00 | 8.00 | 5.17 |
| 5 | GDD/docs/code comments | 1.00 | 2.00 | 3.00 | 2.00 |


## Risk Assessment

- **Risk Score:** 10/25 — **Medium**
- **Probability:** 3.15/5 | **Impact:** 3.15/5

### Top Risk Drivers & Mitigations

1. **Wire into drop draw** — Add targeted tests and integration checks
2. **Tests** — Lock dependencies and add compatibility tests
3. **Shared multiplier + tunables** — Schedule extra review for risky components


## Confidence

- **Confidence:** 76%
- **Unknowns:** Whether a 4x weight at 1 life is gentle enough in practice; may need telemetry/playtest retuning of the base.; Exact hook point for the guaranteed drop relative to the mini-boss death sweep (before vs after) is an implementation detail.
- **Assumptions:** The multiplier scales the extra_life weight inside the existing weighted per-kill pool (Q1a), not the overall drop chance.; runStartingLives is captured at run start (default 3; a hangar deployment may override it); gyms with no run use the catalogue starting lives (3) as the baseline.; The guaranteed mini-boss drop spawns even at the 5-life cap and with a full slot pool (Q2a); the existing gate governs collection.; The asteroid Extra Life roll stays off at the shipped default (0); the multiplier composes with it but is inert there.; The curve is multiplier = 2 ** max(0, runStartingLives - lives) => 1x/2x/4x at 3/2/1 lives (Q3).

intake answers received — Q1: (a) scale the `extra_life` weight in the existing weighted per-kill pool. Q2: (a) always spawn a physical `extra_life` field pickup at the mini-boss death position, in addition to the wheel reward, even at the cap / full slots. Q3: a curve gentler than the offered (b) — `1x / 2x / 4x` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives, i.e. `multiplier = 2 ** max(0, runStartingLives - lives)`.

Asteroid follow-up: **correct — asteroids no longer drop lives at shipped defaults.** `DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE = 0` (AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR / AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM); the rule and persisted key are retained but off. The shared multiplier is defined once and composes with that roll if a designer re-enables it (inert at 0).

Brief finalised and stage advanced to `intake_complete`; effort/risk recorded (Medium / Medium).
